The current build workflow defines `HEVY_API_KEY` at workflow scope, so every
job and step can inherit it even though the PR workflow runs deterministic
mocked integration rather than live integration. Early work must remove this
workflow/job/step inheritance from deterministic lanes. Credentials should
exist only on explicitly credentialed live/manual/nightly/release jobs, never
as ambient workflow configuration for PR tests.

## Coverage policy

### Step 1: fix the denominator

- Define `coverage.include` for repository-owned production TypeScript, for
  example `packages/*/src/**/*.ts`.
- Explicitly exclude generated Kubb files, test files, declarations, and any
  intentionally non-runtime build configuration.
- Decide whether CLI bootstrap modules belong in the unit report, stdio report,
  or a merged report, but ensure they appear in the total denominator.
- Give unit, MCP, and stdio reports Codecov flags or otherwise merge them in a
  reproducible way without double-counting ambiguity.

### Step 2: record the merged-main baseline

Land the denominator change without arbitrary failure thresholds, run it on
merged `main`, and record lines, functions, statements, branches, and uncovered
risk areas. A percentage from the old imported-files-only denominator must not
be used as the new floor.

name: Build and Test

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  ROLLUP_SKIP_NODEJS_NATIVE_BUILD: "true"
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"

jobs:
  upload-source-event:
    name: Upload source event
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Upload source event
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: source-event
          path: ${{ github.event_path }}
          if-no-files-found: error

  build:
    name: Build and test (Node ${{ matrix.node-version }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node-version:
          - "24.x"
          - "26.x"

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}
          cache: "npm"

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Validate repository control plane
        run: npx nx run repository:check:control-plane

      - name: Check package boundaries
        run: npx nx run repository:check:boundaries

      - name: Check package export maps
        run: npx nx run repository:check:exports

      - name: Run type check
        run: npx nx run repository:check:types

      - name: Check server manifest
        run: npx nx run repository:check:server-manifest

      - name: Run Check
        run: npx nx run repository:check

      - name: Verify commit messages
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && matrix.node-version == '24.x'
        run: npx commitlint --from ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} --to ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }} --verbose

      - name: Check for changeset
        if: >-
          github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
          matrix.node-version == '24.x' &&
          github.actor != 'dependabot[bot]' &&
          github.head_ref != 'changeset-release/main'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
        run: |
          npx changeset status --since="origin/${BASE_REF}"
          npx nx run repository:check:package-changesets -- --since "origin/${BASE_REF}"

      - name: Run nightly diagnostics redaction regression tests
        if: matrix.node-version == '24.x'
        run: npx nx run repository:test:diagnostics
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ""

      - name: Run build
        run: npx nx run repository:build
        env:
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
          CODECOV_TOKEN: ${{ matrix.node-version == '24.x' && secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN || '' }}

      - name: Run Worker HTTP integration tests
        if: matrix.node-version == '24.x'
        run: npx nx run repository:test:worker-http

      - name: Run Worker tests
        if: matrix.node-version == '24.x'
        run: npx nx run repository:test:worker

      - name: Run mocked integration tests with coverage
        if: matrix.node-version == '24.x'
        run: npx nx run repository:test:mcp -- --coverage --coverage.reportsDirectory=coverage/mocked

      - name: Run mocked integration tests
        if: matrix.node-version == '26.x'
        run: npx nx run repository:test:mcp

      - name: Run unit tests with coverage and JUnit output
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        run: npx nx run repository:test:unit -- --coverage --coverage.reportsDirectory=coverage/unit --reporter=default --reporter=junit --outputFile.junit=test-results/unit-tests.xml

      - name: Upload test results to Codecov
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@fb8b3582c8e4def4969c97caa2f19720cb33a72f # v7.0.0
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: ./test-results/unit-tests.xml
          disable_search: true
          report_type: test_results

      - name: Run unit tests with coverage
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '26.x' }}
        run: npx nx run repository:test:unit -- --coverage

      - name: Run contract baseline
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        run: npx nx run repository:test:contract

      - name: Run stdio baseline
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        run: npx nx run repository:test:stdio

      - name: Run package and CLI package baselines
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        run: npx nx run repository:test:pack:cli

      - name: Check published package metadata
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        run: npx nx run repository:check:publint

      - name: Run CLI tests
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        run: npx nx run repository:test:cli

      - name: Build and scan Worker dry run
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        run: npx nx run repository:worker:dry-run

      - name: Run performance baseline
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        run: npx nx run repository:test:performance

      - name: Upload performance summary
        if: ${{ always() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: performance-summary-node-24
          path: test-results/performance/summary.json
          if-no-files-found: error

      - name: Upload unit test results
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && matrix.node-version == '24.x' }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: unit-test-results-node-24
          path: test-results/unit-tests.xml
          if-no-files-found: warn

      - name: Upload results to Codecov
        if: matrix.node-version == '24.x'
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@fb8b3582c8e4def4969c97caa2f19720cb33a72f # v7.0.0
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: ./coverage/unit/lcov.info,./coverage/mocked/lcov.info

  docker:
    name: Build and smoke test Docker image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@bb05f3f5519dd87d3ba754cc423b652a5edd6d2c # v4.2.0

      - name: Build Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          load: true
          tags: hevy-mcp:ci

      - name: Smoke test version output without an API key
        run: docker run --rm hevy-mcp:ci --version

      - name: Smoke test help output without an API key
        run: docker run --rm hevy-mcp:ci --help

      - name: Verify hardened runtime structure
        run: |
          docker run --rm --entrypoint sh hevy-mcp:ci -c '
            test "$(id -u)" -ne 0 &&
            test ! -e /app/node_modules &&
            test -f /app/standalone.mjs
          '

  otel-cicd-action:
    if: always()
    name: OpenTelemetry Export Trace
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build, docker]
    env:
      OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - name: Export workflow
        # The collector token exists only in chrisdoc/hevy-mcp, and fork PRs
        # run without secrets — skip the export when the token is absent
        # instead of failing the whole workflow.
        if: env.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN != ''
        uses: corentinmusard/otel-cicd-action@6022e68732c1cab4d2c8218b810f69006ee5cc34 # v4.1.0
        with:
          otlpEndpoint: "https://otel.chrisdoc.dev/v1/traces"
          otlpHeaders: "Authorization=Bearer ${{ env.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}"
          githubToken: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          runId: ${{ github.run_id }}

--- .github/workflows/deploy-worker.yml (390 lines)
name: Deploy Cloudflare Worker Preview

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main
    types:
      - opened
      - reopened
      - synchronize
      - closed

permissions:
  contents: read

env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"

jobs:
  preview:
    name: Deploy PR preview
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      github.event.action != 'closed' &&
      github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]' &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    concurrency:
      group: cloudflare-worker-preview-pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
    environment:
      name: preview
      url: ${{ steps.preview_url.outputs.url }}
    env:
      WRANGLER_MODE: preview
      CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME }}
      CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_ROUTE: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_ROUTE }}
      CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_LOGS_DESTINATIONS: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_LOGS_DESTINATIONS }}
      CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_TRACES_DESTINATIONS: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_TRACES_DESTINATIONS }}
      CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_KV_NAMESPACE_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_KV_NAMESPACE_ID }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout pull request commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Check whether the preview Worker exists
        id: preview_worker
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          response_body="$(mktemp)"
          trap 'rm -f "$response_body"' EXIT

          set +e
          http_status="$(
            curl \
              --silent \
              --show-error \
              --output "$response_body" \
              --write-out "%{http_code}" \
              --connect-timeout 10 \
              --max-time 30 \
              --request GET \
              --header "Authorization: Bearer ${CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN}" \
              --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
              "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/${CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID}/workers/scripts/${CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME}/settings"
          )"
          curl_exit=$?
          set -e

          if (( curl_exit != 0 )); then
            echo "Cloudflare preview Worker existence check failed during transport (curl exit ${curl_exit})." >&2
            exit "$curl_exit"
          fi

          case "$http_status" in
            200)
              echo "bootstrap=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            404)
              echo "bootstrap=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "Cloudflare preview Worker existence check returned unexpected HTTP ${http_status}; refusing to bootstrap." >&2
              exit 1
              ;;
          esac

      - name: Bootstrap dedicated preview Worker
        if: steps.preview_worker.outputs.bootstrap == 'true'
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
        run: >-
          npx wrangler deploy .github/workers/preview-bootstrap.ts
          --x-new-config
          --env preview
          --keep-vars
          --message "Bootstrap inert ${CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME} Worker for GitHub PR versions"

      - name: Resolve preview Worker version tag
        id: worker_version
        run: |
          tag="$(node scripts/resolve-worker-version.mjs preview \
            "${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}" \
            "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}")"
          echo "tag=$tag" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Upload preview version
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          PREVIEW_ALIAS: pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          WRANGLER_OUTPUT_FILE_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/wrangler-output.ndjson
          WORKER_VERSION_TAG: ${{ steps.worker_version.outputs.tag }}
        run: |
          # Truncate to prevent stale entries from a prior run polluting version ID extraction
          : > "${WRANGLER_OUTPUT_FILE_PATH}"
          npx wrangler versions upload \
            --x-new-config \
            --env preview \
            --keep-vars \
            --preview-alias "${PREVIEW_ALIAS}" \
            --tag "${WORKER_VERSION_TAG}" \
            --message "GitHub PR #${PR_NUMBER} at ${HEAD_SHA}"

      - name: Activate preview version
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          WRANGLER_OUTPUT_FILE_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/wrangler-output.ndjson
        run: |
          version_id="$(node <<'NODE'
          const fs = require("node:fs");

          const entries = fs
            .readFileSync(process.env.WRANGLER_OUTPUT_FILE_PATH, "utf8")
            .trim()
            .split("\n")
            .filter(Boolean)
            .map((line) => JSON.parse(line));
          const upload = entries.findLast(
            (entry) => entry.type === "version-upload",
          );
          const versionId = upload?.version_id ?? upload?.id;

          if (!versionId) {
            throw new Error(
              "Wrangler did not return version_id; verify the preview version upload completed successfully",
            );
          }

          process.stdout.write(versionId);
          NODE
          )"
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if npx wrangler versions deploy "$version_id" \
              --x-new-config \
              --env preview \
              --yes \
              --message "Activate GitHub PR #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} preview"; then
              break
            fi
            if [ "$attempt" -lt 3 ]; then
              echo "::warning::wrangler versions deploy attempt ${attempt} failed, retrying in 15s..."
              sleep 15
            else
              echo "::error::All 3 wrangler versions deploy attempts failed."
              exit 1
            fi
          done

      - name: Publish preview URL
        id: preview_url
        env:
          EXPECTED_PREFIX: pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}-${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME }}.
          WRANGLER_OUTPUT_FILE_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/wrangler-output.ndjson
        run: |
          node <<'NODE'
          const fs = require("node:fs");

          const entries = fs
            .readFileSync(process.env.WRANGLER_OUTPUT_FILE_PATH, "utf8")
            .trim()
            .split("\n…3996 tokens truncated… run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          path: artifacts

      - name: Publish unit test results
        if: ${{ hashFiles('artifacts/unit-test-results-node-24/*.xml') != '' }}
        uses: EnricoMi/publish-unit-test-result-action/linux@d0a4676d0e0b938bc201470d88276b7c74c712b3 # v2.24.0
        with:
          github_token: ${{ github.token }}
          commit: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          event_file: artifacts/source-event/event.json
          event_name: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.event }}
          files: artifacts/unit-test-results-node-24/*.xml
          check_name: Unit Test Results
          comment_title: Unit Test Results
          comment_mode: always
--- .github/workflows/release.yml (309 lines)
name: Release

on:
  # This privileged follow-up is gated to a successful push to main from this
  # repository, so it only checks out a trusted commit already tested by CI.
  workflow_run: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
    workflows: ["Build and Test"]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]
permissions: {}

env:
  ROLLUP_SKIP_NODEJS_NATIVE_BUILD: "true"
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"

jobs:
  release:
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # to be able to publish a GitHub release
      issues: write # to be able to comment on released issues
      pull-requests: write # to be able to comment on released pull requests
      id-token: write # to enable use of OIDC for npm provenance
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.release.outputs.version }}
      released: ${{ steps.release.outputs.released }}
      node_released: ${{ steps.release.outputs.node_released }}
      worker_version: ${{ steps.release.outputs.worker_version }}
      worker_released: ${{ steps.release.outputs.worker_released }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: ".nvmrc"
          cache: "npm"
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx nx run repository:build
        env:
          HEVY_MCP_RELEASE: "true"
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
      - name: Run unit tests
        run: npx nx run repository:test:release-unit
      - name: Run Worker tests
        run: npx nx run repository:test:worker
      - name: Run CLI tests
        run: npx nx run repository:test:cli
      - name: Verify published packages
        run: npx nx run repository:test:pack:cli
      - name: Check published package metadata
        run: npx nx run repository:check:publint
        env:
          HEVY_MCP_RELEASE: "true"
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
      - name: Run integration tests
        run: npx nx run repository:test:integration
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HEVY_API_KEY }}

      - name: Test source MCP build
        run: npx nx run repository:test:nightly
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HEVY_API_KEY }}
          HEVY_MCP_COMMAND: node
          HEVY_MCP_ARGS_JSON: '["packages/node/dist/cli.mjs"]'
          HEVY_MCP_LAUNCHER: release-source
          HEVY_MCP_SOURCE_REVISION: ${{ github.sha }}
          HEVY_MCP_DIAGNOSTICS_PATH: test-results/release-source.json

      - name: Smoke test live local Worker HTTP path
        continue-on-error: true
        run: npx nx run repository:test:worker-http:live
        env:
          HEVY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HEVY_API_KEY }}
          HEVY_RUN_LIVE_WORKER_TESTS: "1"

      - name: Create Release PR or Publish
        id: changesets
        uses: changesets/action@2d9f7af6402422be60d377f151c7618011bba45a # v2.0.0-next.4
        with:
          version-script: npx nx run repository:version:changesets
          publish-script: npx nx run repository:release
          commit-message: "chore: version packages"
          pr-title: "chore: version packages"
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          SENTRY_ORG: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_ORG }}
          SENTRY_PROJECT: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_PROJECT }}
          SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN }}
          OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.OTEL_COLLECTOR_TOKEN }}
          HEVY_MCP_RELEASE: "true"
      - name: Set Release Outputs
        id: release
        env:
          PKGS: ${{ steps.changesets.outputs['published-packages'] }}
          PUBLISHED: ${{ steps.changesets.outputs.published }}
          RELEASE_COMMIT: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          node scripts/release-outputs.mjs \
            "$RELEASE_COMMIT^1" \
            "$RELEASE_COMMIT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  publish-container:
    name: Publish Docker image
    needs: release
    if: needs.release.outputs.node_released == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout tested release commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up QEMU
        uses: docker/setup-qemu-action@96fe6ef7f33517b61c61be40b68a1882f3264fb8 # v4.2.0

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@bb05f3f5519dd87d3ba754cc423b652a5edd6d2c # v4.2.0

      - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
        uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Generate Docker image metadata
        id: metadata
        uses: docker/metadata-action@dc802804100637a589fabce1cb79ff13a1411302 # v6.2.0
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}
          flavor: latest=false
          tags: |
            type=raw,value=latest,enable=${{ !contains(needs.release.outputs.version, '-') }}
            type=semver,pattern={{version}},value=${{ needs.release.outputs.version }}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}},value=${{ needs.release.outputs.version }}
            type=semver,pattern={{major}}.{{minor}},value=${{ needs.release.outputs.version }}

      - name: Build and publish Docker image
        uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          platforms: linux/amd64,linux/arm64
          push: true
          tags: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.metadata.outputs.labels }}

  deploy-production:
    name: Deploy production Worker
    needs: release
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main' &&
      needs.release.outputs.worker_released == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: cloudflare-worker-production
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: read
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://hevy.chrisdoc.dev/mcp
    steps:
      - name: Checkout published release commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version-file: .nvmrc
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Deploy published version
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          WRANGLER_MODE: production
          CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_NAME }}
          CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_ROUTE: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_ROUTE }}
          CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_LOGS_DESTINATIONS: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_LOGS_DESTINATIONS }}
          CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_TRACES_DESTINATIONS: ${{ vars.CLOUDFLARE_OTEL_TRACES_DESTINATIONS }}
          CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_KV_NAMESPACE_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_OAUTH_KV_NAMESPACE_ID }}
          RELEASE_COMMIT: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha || github.sha }}
          WORKER_VERSION: ${{ needs.release.outputs.worker_version }}
        run: >-
          npx wrangler deploy
          --x-new-config
          --env production
          --tag "$WORKER_VERSION"
          --message "Changesets release at $RELEASE_COMMIT"

  publish-preview:
    name: Publish hevy-mcp preview
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_branch == 'main' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: npm-preview-main
      cancel-in-progress: true
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout tested commit
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Verify tested commit is current main
        env:
          TESTED_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          checked_out_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          current_main_sha="$(git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main | awk 'NR == 1 { print $1 }')"
          if [ -z "$current_main_sha" ]; then
            echo "Unable to determine the current origin/main SHA"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$checked_out_sha" != "$TESTED_SHA" ] || [ "$current_main_sha" != "$TESTED_SHA" ]; then
            echo "Refusing to publish stale tested commit"
            echo "tested: $TESTED_SHA"
            echo "checked out: $checked_out_sha"
            echo "current main: $current_main_sha"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0

name: Close Stale Issues

on:
  schedule:
    # Run daily at 00:00 UTC
    - cron: "0 0 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch: # Allow manual trigger

permissions:
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

env:
  FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: "true"

jobs:
  stale:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Close stale issues and PRs
        uses: actions/stale@4391f3da665fdf50b6810c1a66712fb9ba21aa93 # v11.0.0
        with:
          # Issues
          stale-issue-message: >-
            This issue has been automatically marked as stale because it has
            not had recent activity. It will be closed if no further activity
            occurs. Thank you for your contributions.
          close-issue-message: >-
            This issue has been automatically closed due to inactivity. If you
            believe this issue is still relevant, please feel free to reopen it
            or create a new one.
          stale-issue-label: "stale"
          days-before-issue-stale: 60
          days-before-issue-close: 7

          # Pull Requests
          stale-pr-message: >-
            This pull request has been automatically marked as stale because it
            has not had recent activity. It will be closed if no further
            activity occurs. Thank you for your contributions.
          close-pr-message: >-
            This pull request has been automatically closed due to inactivity.
            If you believe this PR is still relevant, please feel free to
            reopen it or update it.
          stale-pr-label: "stale"
          days-before-pr-stale: 30
          days-before-pr-close: 7

          # Exempt labels
          exempt-issue-labels: "pinned,security,enhancement"
          exempt-pr-labels: "pinned,security"

          # Only process issues/PRs
          operations-per-run: 30

        with:

          path: token-cost-base
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Prepare comparison baseline
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" != "pull_request" ]]; then
            cp token-cost-baseline.json token-cost-base.json
            exit 0
          fi

          if [[ -f token-cost-base/scripts/measure-token-cost.ts ]] &&
             node -e 'const p=require("./token-cost-base/package.json"); process.exit(p.scripts?.["measure:tokens"] && (p.devDependencies?.tiktoken || p.dependencies?.tiktoken) ? 0 : 1)'; then

        run: >-

          --baseline token-cost-base.json

            token-cost-base.json
            token-cost-report.md

    name: Update pull request comment
    needs: measure

      needs.measure.result == 'success' &&
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&

    permissions:
      contents: read

        uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3 # v9.0.0
        with:
          script: |
            const fs = require("node:fs");
            const marker = "<!-- hevy-mcp-token-cost -->";
            const report = fs.readFileSync("token-cost-report.md", "utf8");
            const body = `${marker}\n<details>\n<summary><strong>MCP tool token cost</strong></summary>\n\n${report}\n</details>`;

              github.rest.issues.listComments,
              {
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                per_page: 100,
              },
            );
            const existing = comments.find(
              (comment) =>
                comment.user?.login === "github-actions[bot]" &&
                comment.body?.includes(marker),
            );

            if (existing) {
              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                comment_id: existing.id,
                body,
              });
            } else {
              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
                owner: context.repo.owner,
                repo: context.repo.repo,
                issue_number: context.issue.number,
                body,
              });
            }

    13	The repository currently has a deliberate Node policy difference:
    14	
    15	- `package.json` declares the published package compatible with Node.js 20 or
    16	  newer.
    17	- Repository development guidance uses the exact version in `.nvmrc`, which is
    18	  Node.js 24 at the current base.
    19	- CI tests Node.js 24 and 26 at the current base, as configured in
    20	  `.github/workflows/build-and-test.yml`.
    21	
    22	Use `.nvmrc` for development unless a change is specifically testing the wider
    23	published compatibility range:
    24	
    25	```bash
    26	nvm use
    27	node --version
    28	npm install
    29	```
    30	
    31	Do not silently change the published Node policy as part of unrelated work.
    32	
    33	## Hevy API key and local environment
    34	
    35	Copy the sample environment when you need to start the server or run live
    36	tests:
    37	
    38	```bash
    39	cp .env.sample .env
    40	```
    41	
    42	Set your key only in `.env` or the process environment:
    43	
    44	```dotenv
    45	HEVY_API_KEY=your-hevy-api-key
    46	```
    47	
    48	- Never commit `.env` or a real API key.
    49	- Never pass the key through CLI arguments, URLs, logs, fixtures, or screenshots.
    50	- Deterministic unit, mocked MCP, contract, stdio, package, and performance
    51	  lanes do not need a live key.
    52	- `npm run test:live` requires `HEVY_API_KEY` and fails its preflight when the
    53	  key is absent.
    54	
    55	## Local development
    56	
    57	Install, build, and start the production stdio executable:
    58	
    59	```bash
    60	npm install
    61	npm run build
    62	npm start
    63	```
    64	
    65	For watch mode:
    66	
    67	```bash
    68	npm run dev
    69	```
    70	
    71	Both commands load `.env` and require `HEVY_API_KEY`. The Node entry point is
    72	stdio-only. It writes MCP JSON-RPC to stdout and diagnostics to stderr; it does
    73	not listen on a port or support `PORT`, `HEVY_MCP_TRANSPORT`, or `--transport`.
    74	Use an MCP client or the inspector rather than typing requests directly into
    75	the terminal.
    76	
    77	Useful inspection commands are:
    78	
    79	```bash
    80	npm run inspect
    81	npm run inspect:npm
    82	```
    83	
    84	The inspector can require an environment with an MCP-capable browser/client and
    85	may time out in restricted environments.

   162	The live integration file under `tests/integration` is credential-gated in its
   163	own implementation, but contributors should use the explicit `test:live` lane
   164	for a real API canary. Do not describe `test:live` as skipped without a key: its
   165	launcher intentionally exits with an error before starting tests.
   166	
   167	The live Worker lane invokes only bounded read paths. It verifies
   168	`search-exercise-templates` registration through `tools/list` without invoking
   169	the full-catalog search against production.
   170	
   171	The normal pull request baseline is:
   172	
   173	```bash
   174	npm run test:pr
   175	npm run test:performance
   176	```
   177	
   178	Performance timing targets are currently informational. Correctness, fixture,
   179	network-isolation, and report-shape failures remain blocking. The versioned
   180	report is written to `test-results/performance/summary.json`.
   181	
   182	## Required validation
   183	
   184	Run these checks before opening a pull request:
   185	
   186	```bash
   187	npm run check
   188	npm run check:types
   189	npm run build
   190	npm run test:pr
   191	npm run test:performance
   192	npm run check:changeset
   193	```
   194	
   195	Also verify the generated contributor projection when changing validation lane
   196	identities, aliases, or aggregate membership:
   197	
   198	```bash
   199	node scripts/render-validation-lanes.mjs
   200	```
   201	
   202	Also run the narrow checks related to your change. In particular:
   203	
   204	- Run `npm run test:stdio` after changes to process lifecycle, stdio transport,
   205	  diagnostics, or the MCP TypeScript SDK.
   206	- Run `npm run test:pack` after package entry point, binary, manifest, or
   207	  published-file changes.
   208	- Run `npm run check:server-manifest` after server metadata changes.
   209	- Run `npm run measure:tokens` when tool descriptions or schemas materially
   210	  change; see [docs/token-cost-tracking.md](./docs/token-cost-tracking.md).
   211	- Run `npm run test:live` only when a real Hevy API canary is appropriate and a
   212	  safe credential is available.
   213	
   214	`npm run check` runs both oxlint and oxfmt in check mode using the local npm
   215	dependencies. The project uses the Oxc tools for fast, consistent type-aware
   216	linting and formatting. Fix reported code warnings rather than assuming they
   217	are harmless. Use `npm run check:fix` for automated fixes, then inspect the
   218	resulting diff. `check:fix` modifies files in the working tree but does not
   219	stage them; review and stage the changes manually. hk uses the same tools for
   220	Git hook execution.

1	# Contributor Onboarding
     2	
     3	Welcome to **hevy-mcp**! 🎉 This guide walks you through your first contribution — from cloning the repository to opening a pull request. It's a practical quick-start companion to the full reference in [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md), which you should keep open for deeper details as you go.
     4	
     5	> [!NOTE]
     6	> This guide focuses on getting you moving quickly. [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md) is the authoritative reference for edge cases, detailed rules, and the full validation matrix.
     7	
     8	## What is hevy-mcp?
     9	
    10	**hevy-mcp** is a [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server for the [Hevy](https://www.hevyapp.com/) fitness API. It lets AI assistants read, analyze, create, and update workouts, routines, exercise templates, and body measurements through the Hevy API. [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)
    11	
    12	The project runs in two very different places:
    13	
    14	- **Locally** — as a Node.js stdio process on a developer's machine
    15	- **Hosted** — as a Cloudflare Worker serving Streamable HTTP to remote clients
    16	
    17	Both deployments run the **same MCP tool contract**, which is the central architectural insight that shapes how the codebase is organized. [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/8d8e965a-36c3-4f95-b2d6-3779bce46661)
    18	
    19	## Quick Setup (5 minutes)
    20	
    21	### 1. Clone and install
    22	
    23	```bash
    24	git clone https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp.git
    25	cd hevy-mcp
    26	nvm use
    27	npm install
    28	npm run build
    29	```
    30	
    31	> [!TIP]
    32	> `nvm use` switches to the exact Node.js version in `.nvmrc` (currently Node 24). CI tests against this version — using it locally keeps your environment consistent. [[3]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)
    33	
    34	### 2. Verify everything works
    35	
    36	```bash
    37	npm run test:unit
    38	```
    39	
    40	You should see all unit tests pass in about 1–2 seconds. [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/8d8e965a-36c3-4f95-b2d6-3779bce46661)
    41	
    42	> [!NOTE]
    43	> **Integration tests require a Hevy API key** and will fail intentionally without one. `npm run test:unit` is fully deterministic and works without any credentials — it's your go-to command during development. If you need to run integration tests later, copy `.env.sample` to `.env` and add your `HEVY_API_KEY`. [[4]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)
    44	
    45	### 3. (Optional) Set up Git hooks
    46

    57	## Understanding the Project Structure
    58	
    59	The repository is a TypeScript monorepo with five workspace packages under `packages/`. The root is a private orchestrator with no runtime source tree — all implementation lives in the workspaces. [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/8d8e965a-36c3-4f95-b2d6-3779bce46661)
    60	
    61	### The five workspaces
    62	
    63	| Workspace               | Package name            | Role                                                                      |
    64	| ----------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    65	| `packages/hevy-client/` | `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` | Runtime-neutral Hevy API client, generated from the OpenAPI spec via Kubb |
    66	| `packages/core/`        | `@hevy-mcp/core`        | MCP tools, prompts, resources — the shared runtime-neutral implementation |
    67	| `packages/node/`        | `hevy-mcp`              | Node.js stdio/HTTP adapter, telemetry, process lifecycle                  |
    68	| `packages/worker/`      | `@hevy-mcp/worker`      | Cloudflare Worker Streamable HTTP and OAuth adapter                       |
    69	| `packages/cli/`         | `@chrisdoc/hevy-cli`    | Public Hevy command-line client                                           |
    70	
    71	[[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/8d8e965a-36c3-4f95-b2d6-3779bce46661)
    72	
    73	### The most important rule: runtime neutrality
    74	
    75	`packages/core` and `packages/hevy-client` **must work on both Node.js and Cloudflare Workers**. This means they cannot use Node.js built-ins (`process`, `fs`, `child_process`, etc.) or Cloudflare-specific bindings. Standard Web APIs only (`fetch`, `URL`, `TextEncoder`, Web Crypto). [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)
    76	
    77	Platform-specific code belongs here:
    78	
    79	- **`packages/node`** — stdio transport, process lifecycle (`SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`), Node telemetry
    80	- **`packages/worker`** — Cloudflare Worker entrypoint, OAuth 2.1 layer, KV bindings
    81	
    82	> [!IMPORTANT]
    83	> The Node adapter (`hevy-mcp`) and the Worker adapter (`@hevy-mcp/worker`) must **never import each other**. The composition graph flows one way: `hevy-client → core → node/worker/CLI`. [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)
    84	
    85	### Key files inside `packages/core/src/`
    86	
    87	```
    88	packages/core/src/
    89	├── tools/                 # MCP tool implementations (+ co-located *.test.ts)
    90	│   ├── annotations.ts
    91	│   ├── body-measurements.ts
    92	│   ├── folders.ts
    93	│   ├── routines.ts
    94	│   ├── templates.ts
    95	│   ├── user.ts
    96	│   └── workouts.ts
    97	└── utils/                 # Shared helpers
    98	    ├── tool-helpers.ts    # InferToolParams type inference utility
    99	    ├── error-handler.ts   # withErrorHandling wrapper
   100	    ├── response-formatter.ts  # Output schemas and MCP response assembly
   101	    └── cache.ts           # Per-server template/cache helpers
   102	```

   105	> For the full runtime architecture and composition graph, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](../CONTRIBUTING.md).

   107	## Which Tests to Run When
   108	
   109	The repository has 20+ test lanes. Here's a practical grouping so you know exactly what to run and when. [[5]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/01d1e0ea12f26ff22f8967f52b5577fae7fc03b9/docs/test-lanes.md)
   110	
   111	### Daily development — always run these
   112	
   113	```bash
   114	npm run test:unit      # Fast unit tests, no credentials needed (~1-2 seconds)
   115	npm run test:mcp       # Mocked MCP integration tests, no credentials needed
   116	```
   117	
   118	These two lanes are deterministic and form the core feedback loop during development. [[6]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/01d1e0ea12f26ff22f8967f52b5577fae7fc03b9/docs/test-lanes.md#L60-L75)
   119	
   120	### Before opening a PR — run all of these
   121	
   122	```bash
   123	npm run test:pr           # Full deterministic PR baseline (runs unit, mocked MCP, contract, stdio, worker, worker-http, pack, and more)
   124	npm run test:performance  # Performance checks — currently informational, not a blocking gate
   125	npm run check:changeset   # Verify your changeset file is correct
   126	```
   127	
   128	> [!TIP]
   129	> `npm run test:pr` is the single most important pre-PR command. It runs 10 deterministic lanes in one shot and is what CI checks. `npm run test:performance` writes a report to `test-results/performance/summary.json` — timing targets are informational today, but correctness failures are blocking. [[7]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/01d1e0ea12f26ff22f8967f52b5577fae7fc03b9/docs/test-lanes.md#L79-L86) [[8]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/01d1e0ea12f26ff22f8967f52b5577fae7fc03b9/docs/test-lanes.md#L158-L175)

   133	| Command                    | When to run                                                                                      |
   134	| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

   136	| `npm run test:pack`        | After changes to package entry points, binary mapping, or published files                        |
   137	| `npm run test:live`        | Only with a valid `HEVY_API_KEY` — runs a read-only canary against the real Hevy API             |

   340	## Git Workflow
   341	
   342	### Branch from latest `origin/main`
   343	
   344	Always start fresh from the latest `origin/main` — never work from a stale local branch:
   345	
   346	```bash
   347	git fetch origin
   348	git checkout -b feat/my-feature origin/main
   349	```
   350	
   351	Never commit directly to `main` — branch protection blocks it. [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/8d8e965a-36c3-4f95-b2d6-3779bce46661)
   352	
   353	### Use Conventional Commits
   354	
   355	All commits must use the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format: [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/8d8e965a-36c3-4f95-b2d6-3779bce46661)
   356	
   357	```
   358	feat: add get-workout-streak tool
   359	fix: handle missing exercise template gracefully
   360	docs: update contributor onboarding guide
   361	test: add unit tests for response formatter
   362	refactor: extract pagination helper
   363	build: upgrade MCP TypeScript SDK
   364	ci: add worker-http lane to PR aggregate
   365	chore: update dev dependencies
   366	```
   367	
   368	### Never bypass Git hooks
   369	
   370	The pre-commit, commit-msg, and pre-push hooks run formatting, linting, unit tests, and changeset checks automatically. Never use `--no-verify`. Fix the underlying failure instead. [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/8d8e965a-36c3-4f95-b2d6-3779bce46661)
   371

   380	   ```
   381	
   382	2. **TypeScript type checking:**

   387

   394	4. **Full PR test baseline:**

This is your safety net — but running the checks manually first makes the push faster and avoids surprises.    412	## Troubleshooting Common Issues
   413	
   414	### "Build fails with formatting or linting errors"
   415	
   416	Run the formatter/linter to identify problems:
   417	
   418	```bash
   419	npm run check
   420	```
   421	
   422	For automated fixes, use:
   423	
   424	```bash
   425	npm run check:fix
   426	```
   427	
   428	Review the diff before staging — `check:fix` modifies files but does not stage them. [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)
   429	
   430	---
   431	
   432	### "TypeScript errors inside `packages/hevy-client/src/generated/`"
   433	
   434	This is **expected**. The generated client directory contains auto-generated TypeScript that may have known type errors from the upstream OpenAPI spec. Do not patch these files by hand. If a fix is needed, add it to `scripts/openapi-spec.js` so it survives future regenerations. [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/8d8e965a-36c3-4f95-b2d6-3779bce46661)
   435	
   436	---
   437	
   438	### "Integration tests fail without an API key"
   439	
   440	This is **by design**. `npm run test:live` exits with an error before Vitest even starts when `HEVY_API_KEY` is absent. For deterministic testing during development, use: [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)
   441	
   442	```bash
   443	npm run test:unit    # unit tests only
   444	npm run test:mcp     # mocked MCP integration tests
   445	```
   446	
   447	---
   448	
   449	### "`npm run openapi` fails with `ENOTFOUND`"
   450	
   451	This is **expected in sandboxed environments**. The command fetches the live Hevy OpenAPI spec from `api.hevyapp.com` and cannot reach it without network access. If you're working on a client regeneration locally, make sure you have outbound network access before running this command. [[2]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/8d8e965a-36c3-4f95-b2d6-3779bce46661)
   452	
   453	---
   454	
   455	### "Git hook failures on commit or push"
   456	
   457	If your Git hooks aren't running or are failing with unexpected errors, re-install them:
   458	
   459	```bash
   460	mise install
   461	mise exec hk -- hk install --mise
   462	```
   463	
   464	This sets up the hk-managed hooks (formatting, unit tests, commit message linting, and pre-push validation) without requiring mise to be fully activated in your shell. [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)
   465	
   466	---
   467	
   468	### "TypeScript errors in tool handlers"
   469	
   470	If you're seeing type errors like `Property 'x' does not exist on type 'Record<string, unknown>'`, you likely need to use the `InferToolParams` pattern:
   471	
   472	```typescript
   473	import type { InferToolParams } from "../utils/tool-helpers.js";
   474	
   475	const mySchema = { param: z.string() } as const;
   476	type MyParams = InferToolParams<typeof mySchema>;
   477	```
   478	
   479	See [TYPE_SAFETY_GUIDE.md](./TYPE_SAFETY_GUIDE.md) for the complete pattern and how to find the correct generated response types. [[11]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/01d1e0ea12f26ff22f8967f52b5577fae7fc03b9/docs/TYPE_SAFETY_GUIDE.md#L1-L50)

     1	# Nx and dependency-cruiser control-plane migration
     2	
     3	This stacked follow-up targets PR #890 and moves local repository orchestration
     4	onto Nx plus dependency-cruiser. The canonical repository models own policy
     5	facts; Nx owns project discovery, target invocation, dependency ordering,
     6	affected selection, and cache policy. Root npm aliases remain compatibility
     7	entrypoints for contributors and external automation, not a second owner of
     8	aggregate membership or workflow orchestration. GitHub permissions,
     9	environments, deployment mechanics, and Changesets remain explicit owners where
    10	they carry credentials or release policy.
    11	
    12	## Run the proof of concept
    13	
    14	Nx discovers the five npm workspaces from `packages/*` and the root
    15	`repository` project from `project.json`:
    16	
    17	```sh
    18	npx nx show projects
    19	npx nx show project repository --json
    20	npx nx graph --file=.nx/project-graph.html
    21	```
    22	
    23	The graph file is an inspection artifact under ignored `.nx/`; do not commit
    24	it. To inspect the task graph without writing a graph file, use:
    25	
    26	```sh
    27	npx nx report
    28	npx nx show project repository --json
    29	```
    30	
    31	Run the control-plane aggregate and an explicit clean-base affected query with
    32	no dependency on a dirty local `main`:
    33	
    34	```sh
    35	npx nx run repository:control-plane
    36	npx nx affected --target=control-plane --base=origin/main --head=HEAD
    37	```
    38	
    39	The aggregate target and member identities come from the canonical validation
    40	lane model. The generated contributor tables in
    41	[`docs/test-lanes.md`](./test-lanes.md) show the current lane and aggregate
    42	membership, while `project.json` is the source for target dependencies. Do not
    43	copy a target or member count into prose: derive the current graph with
    44	`npx nx show project repository --json` (or `npx nx graph`). Root aliases remain
    45	supported compatibility entrypoints; workflow steps invoke the corresponding
    46	Nx targets, so command text is not duplicated in the policy model.
    47	
    48	Run the dependency rules independently, through the combined boundary lane,
    49	and exercise the representative pack target:
    50	
    51	```sh
    52	npm run check:dependency-cruiser
    53	npm run check:boundaries
    54	npx nx run repository:check:dependency-cruiser
    55	npx nx run repository:check:boundaries
    56	npx nx run repository:pack:artifacts --skip-nx-cache
    57	```
    58	
    59	The pack target builds the publishable Node server and CLI before writing
    60	`.nx/pack/hevy-mcp-*.tgz` and `.nx/pack/chrisdoc-hevy-cli-*.tgz`. This is
    61	representative artifact metadata only: Node and CLI npm packs are exercised;
    62	Worker and Docker candidate provenance is absent.
    63	
    64	The dependency-cruiser test fixture proves that representative neutral Node
    65	builtin, neutral-to-Node, and Worker observability imports fail closed:
    66	
    67	```sh
    68	npx vitest run scripts/control-plane-config.test.ts
    69	```
    70	
    71	## Migration contract
    72	
    73	- Nx target metadata and executors own local task orchestration, including
    74	  inputs, outputs, cacheability, dependency ordering, and aggregate invocation.
    75	  Root npm scripts remain compatibility aliases where they are retained; they
    76	  are not an independent aggregate registry.
    77	- Deterministic checks and test lanes may be cached; live integration, nightly,
    78	  release/version, package, Worker deployment/dry-run, performance, and
    79	  token-cost targets are explicitly non-cacheable.
    80	- Worker and package smoke lanes opt out of Nx task parallelism because they
    81	  exercise shared local runtimes and publishable output directories.
    82	- Vitest and token-cost arguments pass through Nx with `npx nx run ... -- ...`;
    83	  no workflow needs to depend on undocumented Nx executor internals.
    84	- `npm ci`, Docker actions, Wrangler deployment commands, Changesets actions,
    85	  commit verification, secrets, and environment gates remain explicit because
    86	  they are infrastructure or release policy rather than local project graph
    87	  concerns.
    88	
    89	## What this demonstrates alongside PR #889
    90	
    91	- The canonical `repository/` models own workspace identities, publishability,
    92	  release policy, artifact provenance, and validation lanes. Nx projects and
    93	  targets consume those facts for local graph execution; the generated lane
    94	  documentation is a projection, not another policy registry.
    95	- Nx target metadata and its task graph now own local task orchestration. The
    96	  build/test, nightly, release-local, and token-cost workflows invoke Nx
    97	  targets; no workflow trigger, matrix, permission, secret, or deployment
    98	  condition was changed.
    99	- dependency-cruiser supplies a library-backed module graph and declarative
   100	  package/runtime restrictions instead of another custom graph walker. The
   101	  compiler-backed boundary checker remains authoritative.
   102	- Target metadata records representative inputs and outputs: Kubb generated
   103	  client sources, emitted `dist` directories only for publishable package
   104	  builds, Node build output, server/plugin manifests, coverage and performance
   105	  evidence, and the explicit npm-pack target described above. Type-check-only
   106	  workspace builds declare no output because they are side-effect free.
   107	
   108	This is a local orchestration migration, not a universal runtime/product
   109	manifest. PR #889's `repository/` control-plane implementation is the canonical
   110	policy source for this branch; consumer checks and documentation must read it
   111	through the shared facade rather than maintaining duplicate registries.
   112	
   113	## Evidence from this migration
   114	
   115	| Evidence                            | Current migration result                                                                                         |
   116	| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   117	| Canonical validation policy         | `repository/validation-lanes.json`, projected by `scripts/render-validation-lanes.mjs`                           |
   118	| Current aggregate and target counts | Derived at check time from the lane model and `project.json`; see `npx nx show project repository --json`        |
   119	| Current workflow command ownership  | Workflows invoke Nx targets; credentials, matrices, permissions, and deployment conditions remain workflow-owned |
   120	| Historical migration measurements   | Not repeated here; preserve only as immutable before-adoption evidence when a comparison is required             |
   121	
   122	The current target graph and aggregate membership are intentionally derived
   123	instead of copied into this document. This avoids presenting a stale execution
   124	count as if it were a live measurement.
   125	
   126	## What remains custom
   127	
   128	- Curated package export maps, generated-client closure, and server/plugin
   129	  manifest synchronization remain owned by their existing scripts.
   130	- Release candidate selection, bundled Changeset cascades, empty-Changeset
   131	  policy, and release publication remain Changesets/repository policy rather
   132	  than Nx metadata.
   133	- Credentials, live-network gates, release selectors, Docker actions, and exact
   134	  GitHub matrix/job/step conditions remain workflow-owned. Only local command
   135	  invocation moved to Nx.
   136	- The token-cost job intentionally keeps its base-revision fallback on the npm
   137	  alias because that checkout may predate Nx; the current revision uses Nx.
   138	- Historical before/after execution evidence is not inferable from Nx. Any

This means they cannot use Node.js built-ins (`process`, `fs`, `child_process`, etc.) or Cloudflare-specific bindings. Standard Web APIs only (`fetch`, `URL`, `TextEncoder`, Web Crypto). [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)
    76	
    77	Platform-specific code belongs here:
    78	
    79	- **`packages/node`** — stdio transport, process lifecycle (`SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`), Node telemetry
    80	- **`packages/worker`** — Cloudflare Worker entrypoint, OAuth 2.1 layer, KV bindings
    81	
    82	> [!IMPORTANT]
    83	> The Node adapter (`hevy-mcp`) and the Worker adapter (`@hevy-mcp/worker`) must **never import each other**. The composition graph flows one way: `hevy-client → core → node/worker/CLI`. [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)

   107	## Which Tests to Run When
   108	
   109	The repository has 20+ test lanes. Here's a practical grouping so you know exactly what to run and when. [[5]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/01d1e0ea12f26ff22f8967f52b5577fae7fc03b9/docs/test-lanes.md)

   108	
   109	The repository has 20+ test lanes. Here's a practical grouping so you know exactly what to run and when. [[5]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/01d1e0ea12f26ff22f8967f52b5577fae7fc03b9/docs/test-lanes.md)
   110	
   111	### Daily development — always run these
   112	
   113	```bash
   114	npm run test:unit      # Fast unit tests, no credentials needed (~1-2 seconds)
   115	npm run test:mcp       # Mocked MCP integration tests, no credentials needed
   116	```
   117	
   118	These two lanes are deterministic and form the core feedback loop during development. [[6]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/01d1e0ea12f26ff22f8967f52b5577fae7fc03b9/docs/test-lanes.md#L60-L75)
   119	
   120	### Before opening a PR — run all of these
   121	
   122	```bash
   123	npm run test:pr           # Full deterministic PR baseline (runs unit, mocked MCP, contract, stdio, worker, worker-http, pack, and more)
   124	npm run test:performance  # Performance checks — currently informational, not a blocking gate
   125	npm run check:changeset   # Verify your changeset file is correct
   126	```
   127	
   128	> [!TIP]
   129	> `npm run test:pr` is the single most important pre-PR command. It runs 10 deterministic lanes in one shot and is what CI checks. `npm run test:performance` writes a report to `test-results/performance/summary.json` — timing targets are informational today, but correctness failures are blocking. [[7]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/01d1e0ea12f26ff22f8967f52b5577fae7fc03b9/docs/test-lanes.md#L79-L86) [[8]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/01d1e0ea12f26ff22f8967f52b5577fae7fc03b9/docs/test-lanes.md#L158-L175)
   130	
   131	### Situational — run when relevant
   132	
   133	| Command                    | When to run                                                                                      |
   134	| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
   135	| `npm run test:stdio`       | After changes to process lifecycle, stdio transport, diagnostics, or MCP TypeScript SDK upgrades |
   136	| `npm run test:pack`        | After changes to package entry points, binary mapping, or published files                        |
   137	| `npm run test:live`        | Only with a valid `HEVY_API_KEY` — runs a read-only canary against the real Hevy API             |
   138	| `npm run test:worker`      | After changes to the Cloudflare Worker                                                           |
   139	| `npm run test:worker-http` | After changes to the Cloudflare Worker HTTP integration                                          |
   140	
   141	[[6]](https://github.com/chrisdoc/hevy-mcp/blob/01d1e0ea12f26ff22f8967f52b5577fae7fc03b9/docs/test-lanes.md#L60-L75) [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)
   142	
   143	> [!IMPORTANT]
   144	> `npm run test:live` **does not skip gracefully** without an API key — it exits with an error before Vitest even starts. Use `npm run test:unit` for deterministic testing. [[1]](https://app.dosu.dev/documents/52dd122f-29f8-46dd-9513-3476b4dbb3ae)

     1	# Nx and dependency-cruiser control-plane migration
     2	
     3	This stacked follow-up targets PR #890 and moves local repository orchestration
     4	onto Nx plus dependency-cruiser. The canonical repository models own policy
     5	facts; Nx owns project discovery, target invocation, dependency ordering,
     6	affected selection, and cache policy. Root npm aliases remain compatibility
     7	entrypoints for contributors and external automation, not a second owner of
     8	aggregate membership or workflow orchestration. GitHub permissions,
     9	environments, deployment mechanics, and Changesets remain explicit owners where
    10	they carry credentials or release policy.
    11	
    12	## Run the proof of concept
    13	
    14	Nx discovers the five npm workspaces from `packages/*` and the root
    15	`repository` project from `project.json`:
    16	
    17	```sh
    18	npx nx show projects
    19	npx nx show project repository --json
    20	npx nx graph --file=.nx/project-graph.html
    21	```
    22	
    23	The graph file is an inspection artifact under ignored `.nx/`; do not commit
    24	it. To inspect the task graph without writing a graph file, use:
    25	
    26	```sh
    27	npx nx report
    28	npx nx show project repository --json
    29	```
    30	
    31	Run the control-plane aggregate and an explicit clean-base affected query with
    32	no dependency on a dirty local `main`:
    33	
    34	```sh
    35	npx nx run repository:control-plane
    36	npx nx affected --target=control-plane --base=origin/main --head=HEAD
    37	```
    38	
    39	The aggregate target and member identities come from the canonical validation
    40	lane model. The generated contributor tables in
    41	[`docs/test-lanes.md`](./test-lanes.md) show the current lane and aggregate
    42	membership, while `project.json` is the source for target dependencies. Do not
    43	copy a target or member count into prose: derive the current graph with
    44	`npx nx show project repository --json` (or `npx nx graph`). Root aliases remain
    45	supported compatibility entrypoints; workflow steps invoke the corresponding
    46	Nx targets, so command text is not duplicated in the policy model.
    47	
    48	Run the dependency rules independently, through the combined boundary lane,
    49	and exercise the representative pack target:
    50	
    51	```sh
    52	npm run check:dependency-cruiser
    53	npm run check:boundaries
    54	npx nx run repository:check:dependency-cruiser
    55	npx nx run repository:check:boundaries
    56	npx nx run repository:pack:artifacts --skip-nx-cache
    57	```
    58	
    59	The pack target builds the publishable Node server and CLI before writing
    60	`.nx/pack/hevy-mcp-*.tgz` and `.nx/pack/chrisdoc-hevy-cli-*.tgz`. This is
    61	representative artifact metadata only: Node and CLI npm packs are exercised;
    62	Worker and Docker candidate provenance is absent.
    63	
    64	The dependency-cruiser test fixture proves that representative neutral Node
    65	builtin, neutral-to-Node, and Worker observability imports fail closed:
    66	
    67	```sh
    68	npx vitest run scripts/control-plane-config.test.ts
    69	```
    70	
    71	## Migration contract
    72	
    73	- Nx target metadata and executors own local task orchestration, including
    74	  inputs, outputs, cacheability, dependency ordering, and aggregate invocation.
    75	  Root npm scripts remain compatibility aliases where they are retained; they
    76	  are not an independent aggregate registry.
    77	- Deterministic checks and test lanes may be cached; live integration, nightly,
    78	  release/version, package, Worker deployment/dry-run, performance, and
    79	  token-cost targets are explicitly non-cacheable.
    80	- Worker and package smoke lanes opt out of Nx task parallelism because they
    81	  exercise shared local runtimes and publishable output directories.
    82	- Vitest and token-cost arguments pass through Nx with `npx nx run ... -- ...`;
    83	  no workflow needs to depend on undocumented Nx executor internals.
    84	- `npm ci`, Docker actions, Wrangler deployment commands, Changesets actions,
    85	  commit verification, secrets, and environment gates remain explicit because
    86	  they are infrastructure or release policy rather than local project graph
    87	  concerns.
    88	
    89	## What this demonstrates alongside PR #889
    90	
    91	- The canonical `repository/` models own workspace identities, publishability,
    92	  release policy, artifact provenance, and validation lanes. Nx projects and
    93	  targets consume those facts for local graph execution; the generated lane
    94	  documentation is a projection, not another policy registry.
    95	- Nx target metadata and its task graph now own local task orchestration. The
    96	  build/test, nightly, release-local, and token-cost workflows invoke Nx
    97	  targets; no workflow trigger, matrix, permission, secret, or deployment
    98	  condition was changed.
    99	- dependency-cruiser supplies a library-backed module graph and declarative
   100	  package/runtime restrictions instead of another custom graph walker. The
   101	  compiler-backed boundary checker remains authoritative.
   102	- Target metadata records representative inputs and outputs: Kubb generated
   103	  client sources, emitted `dist` directories only for publishable package
   104	  builds, Node build output, server/plugin manifests, coverage and performance
   105	  evidence, and the explicit npm-pack target described above. Type-check-only
   106	  workspace builds declare no output because they are side-effect free.
   107	
   108	This is a local orchestration migration, not a universal runtime/product
   109	manifest. PR #889's `repository/` control-plane implementation is the canonical
   110	policy source for this branch; consumer checks and documentation must read it
   111	through the shared facade rather than maintaining duplicate registries.
   112	
   113	## Evidence from this migration
   114	
   115	| Evidence                            | Current migration result                                                                                         |
   116	| ----------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   117	| Canonical validation policy         | `repository/validation-lanes.json`, projected by `scripts/render-validation-lanes.mjs`                           |
   118	| Current aggregate and target counts | Derived at check time from the lane model and `project.json`; see `npx nx show project repository --json`        |
   119	| Current workflow command ownership  | Workflows invoke Nx targets; credentials, matrices, permissions, and deployment conditions remain workflow-owned |
   120	| Historical migration measurements   | Not repeated here; preserve only as immutable before-adoption evidence when a comparison is required             |
   121	
   122	The current target graph and aggregate membership are intentionally derived
   123	instead of copied into this document. This avoids presenting a stale execution
   124	count as if it were a live measurement.
   125	
   126	## What remains custom
   127	
   128	- Curated package export maps, generated-client closure, and server/plugin
   129	  manifest synchronization remain owned by their existing scripts.
   130	- Release candidate selection, bundled Changeset cascades, empty-Changeset
   131	  policy, and release publication remain Changesets/repository policy rather
   132	  than Nx metadata.
   133	- Credentials, live-network gates, release selectors, Docker actions, and exact
   134	  GitHub matrix/job/step conditions remain workflow-owned. Only local command
   135	  invocation moved to Nx.
   136	- The token-cost job intentionally keeps its base-revision fallback on the npm
   137	  alias because that checkout may predate Nx; the current revision uses Nx.
   138	- Historical before/after execution evidence is not inferable from Nx. Any
   139	  retained number must be labeled immutable before-adoption evidence; current
   140	  counts are derived from the canonical model and project graph.
   141	- The compiler-backed `check-package-boundaries.mjs` remains authoritative in
   142	  the combined Nx `check:boundaries` target. dependency-cruiser v18 does not
   143	  support this repository's TypeScript 7 compiler, so the migration uses its SWC
   144	  parser; local literal test imports are allowed while the compiler checker
   145	  still rejects non-literal dynamic loading and all runtime-forbidden imports.
   146	  The dependency-cruiser fixture also verifies that the module graph rejects a
   147	  circular workspace edge.
   148	
   149	## Install-script review
   150	
   151	Nx's postinstall checks the platform and only touches Nx Cloud when it is
   152	configured; Nx Cloud is not configured here. SWC's postinstall validates its
   153	native binding and may install a matching `@swc/wasm` fallback. `allowScripts`
   154	remains unchanged. Production adoption therefore still needs an explicit
   155	policy decision about install-time behavior rather than silently broadening
   156	the current dependency policy.
   157	
   158	## Recommendation
   159	
   160	Keep Nx as the local project/task graph and affected selector. Retain the
   161	narrow policy and artifact checks, Changesets, GitHub security controls, and
   162	Cloudflare deployment paths as explicit owners.
